ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: on the left side of the image is an enol fragment; the enol carbon is connected to HO and R1, the double bond extends to the adjacent carbon, and then connects to a carbon bearing R2 and R3 substituents; on the right side of the image is a benzo-fused iodine-containing five-membered-ring reagent, containing a lactone carbonyl, an epoxy connection to iodine, and the iodine also has =O and OH. Between the two there are only curved arrows indicating electron transfer, and no covalent connection is drawn. Then reason: according to the problem statement, ignore the arrows, and R1, R2, R3 are all represented by the wildcard *. The left enol fragment is written according to the specified double-bond configuration as */C(O)=C/C(*)*. The right cyclic iodine reagent is traced from the lactone carbonyl and the O-I-aromatic-ring fused structure, written as O=C1OI(=O)(O)c2ccccc21. Since the left and right two species are not connected, connect the two SMILES with a dot.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: Convert the left enol fragment first: represent R1, R2, and R3 as wildcard atoms and trace the chain as */C(O)=C/C(*)*, preserving the drawn alkene stereochemistry. Then convert the right cyclic iodine reagent by tracing the lactone carbonyl and five-membered O-I-aryl ring fused to benzene, giving O=C1OI(=O)(O)c2ccccc21. Since the two drawn species are not connected and arrows are ignored, concatenate the two SMILES with a dot to obtain */C(O)=C/C(*)*.O=C1OI(=O)(O)c2ccccc21.
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左侧是一个烯醇片段，烯醇碳连有 HO 和 R1，双键延伸到相邻碳，再连接到带有 R2、R3 取代基的碳；图中右侧是一个苯并稠合的含碘五元环试剂，含有内酯羰基、环氧连接到碘，碘上还有 =O 和 OH。两者之间只有弯箭头表示电子转移，没有画出共价连接。再推理：按题意忽略箭头，R1、R2、R3 都用通配符 * 表示。左侧烯醇片段按指定双键构型写为 */C(O)=C/C(*)*。右侧环状碘试剂从内酯羰基和 O-I-芳环稠合结构追踪，写为 O=C1OI(=O)(O)c2ccccc21。由于左右两个物种未连接，用点号连接两个 SMILES。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the straightforward direct-transcription route: identify each drawn chemical fragment in the image, ignore the curved arrows as instructed, and encode the two disconnected structures into SMILES separated by a dot.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the molecular line drawing: the left fragment is an enol/alkene with HO on the left alkene carbon, generic R1 attached to that same carbon, the double bond to the next carbon, and a saturated carbon bearing generic R2 and R3 substituents; the right fragment is an o-iodoxybenzoic acid/benziodoxolone-type cyclic iodine(V) reagent with a lactone carbonyl, ring oxygen, iodine bonded to aryl carbon, one I=O, and one I-OH. Ignore the curved electron-pushing arrows.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text only to determine the required output format, namely the SMILES expression, and to apply the instruction to ignore the arrows rather than treating them as bonds or reaction steps.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard skeletal-structure-to-SMILES rules: unlabeled vertices are carbons, R groups are represented by wildcard atoms '*', disconnected components are joined with '.', drawn alkene geometry can be encoded with '/' markers, and ring closures/fused benzene are encoded with numbered ring atoms.
